newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity mixed ahead of Friday expiry.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity mixed ahead of Friday expiry.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were mixed Friday, with California Oregon Border (COB) up sharply in thin volume on some shortcovering and talk of some contraint in Northwest power offers, industry sources said.
"There is just more COB buyers than sellers out there right now," said a New York based futures trader.

As of 1240 EDT, May COB was up 55 cents at $14.45 after trading as high as $14.70 and as low as $14.10 per megawatt hour (MWh), while June was up 74 cents at $13.45 after exchange as low as $12.75 per MWh.
May Palo Verde (PV) was up two cents at $18.00 after exchanges in a range of $17.80-18.20, while June was down 20 cents at $18.10 after exchanges at $18.00-18.40 per MWh.
August PV had traded down 10 cents at $25.00 after trades at $24.80-25.10 per MWh.
NYMEX said that as of 1210 an estimated total of 149 COB and 391 PV contracts had sold.
Both May COB and PV contracts expire today.

Some support for COB futures was seen from news that Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) may not have surplus power to offer during peak demand hours next month due mainly to earlier block power sales.
BPA has offered some heavy-load power so far this month, but not during "super peak" early morning and evening hours.
"We won't have anything for April and it looks like we might not have any in May," said a BPA trader.

Also in the West, the board of the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) approved a plan to increase capacity limits on the Pacific Intertie to 7,200 megawatts (MW) from the current rate of 6,250 MW, the reliability council said Friday.
The proposal will still need to be reviewed by the full membership of the WSCC, which has 10 days to do so.
BPA had requested increasing the rating to 7,700 MW.
Also, BPA said Friday is had slightly lowered surplus power prices for Monday delivery to $13.00 per MWh for hours ending 1200-1800 PDT in the Northwest.
As of 1245 EDT, NYMEX June Henry Hub natural gas futures were little changed, trading up 0.3 cents at $2.125 per million British thermal units.
Physical power prices in the U.S. West eased this week on moderate weather and the return to service of some generating capacity.

However, several units were expected to cut power as the spring maintenance season continued. A number of units were heard shutting this weekend, including a 700 MW unit at the Colstrip coal-fired complex in Montana and a 550 MW unit at the Laramie River Station in Wyoming.
Forecasts called for Northwest temperatures to average above normal this weekend and into early next week, while in the Southwest, readings would moderate to near normal levels regionwide.
The northern and eastern sections of the Southwest would continue to see cloudy skies with showers and thunderstorms in the valleys and snow in the upper mountains through tomorrow.
COB open interest for April 24 fell 82 to 4,402, while PV open interest rose 65 to 5,551, NYMEX said.
((--Chris Reese, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1627))
